headline: Kuaishou's Kling AI has released Kling 4.0, an AI video model that lets creators steer characters and shots across clips of up to 30 seconds.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a fresh launch from one of China's leading AI video makers, but the capabilities are the company's description and TechNode says results will vary with scene complexity.
importance_line: Film-makers, advertisers and other video creators get more control over AI video, and rival video-model makers face pressure to compete on control as well as looks, but the gains are described by the company and TechNode says they will depend on how complex the scenes are.
summary: TechNode reports that Kling 4.0, the new AI video model from Kling AI (the video service of the Chinese short-video company Kuaishou), can generate up to 30 seconds of video in one go and accepts up to 15 reference files (images, video and audio) plus up to 10 keyframes, which are set points that tell the model how a character or scene should change; Pandaily adds that the model moved from a September preview to general availability on klingai.com. A Kling spokesperson told TechNode that keeping characters, settings and camera work consistent over longer clips is now harder than producing one good-looking shot, so competition is shifting from image quality to control, while TechNode's own assessment is that the tools may cut repeated re-runs but that story, shot choice and final editing still need human judgment.
notes: Full TechNode text read; general-rollout context from Pandaily (16 Oct 2026). Kling 4.0 was previewed in September 2026 (Pandaily); the 16 Oct 2026 general rollout is the event of this entry, so freshness NEW.
